categories.title: HTTP and servers
categories.description: Building and calling web services: routing requests to actions, the request and response values, server runtimes, HTTP clients, WebSockets and API descriptions.

categories.title: Networking and protocols
categories.description: Protocols beyond HTTP and the names behind them: DNS servers, domain parsing, mail transport, MQTT and NATS, and choosing between endpoints.

categories.title: Data and storage
categories.description: Keeping data: databases and the queries over them, caches, files and the images and archives stored in them, and moving data between services.

categories.title: Messaging and jobs
categories.description: Work that happens outside the request: task queues, in-process events, notifications to users, and schedules that dispatch jobs.

categories.title: Security and identity
categories.description: Who is calling and how often: password hashing, sessions, tokens, OAuth2 and passkeys, and limits that keep usage within bounds.

categories.title: Parsing and validation
categories.description: Turning untrusted input into values an application can trust: request parameters, connection strings, email addresses, user agents and translations.

categories.title: Runtime and infrastructure
categories.description: What every service runs on: configuration, dependency injection, command line tools, locks and connection pools, the host system, containers and resilience.

categories.title: Observability
categories.description: Knowing what a service did: audit logs, usage metrics, spans and telemetry exporters.

categories.title: Integrations and AI
categories.description: Connecting to the outside world: version control providers and their webhooks, and AI agents.

categories.title: Engine support
categories.description: Foundations the Rust crates share to behave exactly like PHP: the engine's value model, string and number semantics, regular expressions, JSON and dates.
